facts.text: Dana Point takes its name from a headland that honored author Richard Henry Dana Jr., who first described the harbor in his book Two Years Before the Mast.
In 2019 Dana Point was officially trademarked as the Dolphin and Whale Watching Capital of the World®, and it earned Whale Heritage Site status in 2021.
California Historical Landmark #189 marks the site of the original San Juan Capistrano mission’s Acjachemen village, Toovannga, near Dana Point Harbor.
Dana Point first appeared as an unincorporated community in the 1960 U.S. Census, before becoming an incorporated city in 1997.
The Strands at Headlands, a luxury development on former Chandler family land, showcases Spanish‑style architecture that echoes Dana Point’s early 20th‑century heritage.
